rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The visible positions of the two armies and the caravan show that victory comes from God, not numerical strength or material means.
rows.anchor: ليعلم الخلق أن النصر والغلبة لا تكون بالكثرة والأسباب بل بالله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists held the better, watered far bank; the Muslims were on soft, waterless ground where feet sank, while the caravan was behind the enemy despite their greater numbers and equipment.
rows.anchor: وكان العير وراء ظهور العدو مع كثرة عددهم وعدتعهم وقلة المسليمن وضعفهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears their words and knows the unbeliever's disbelief and punishment and the believer's faith and reward.
rows.anchor: بكفر من كفر وعقابه وبايمان من آمن وثوابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These were another group who, unlike others, made no false excuses for staying behind but confessed their fault and regretted it.
rows.anchor: لم يعتذروا من تخلفهم بالمعاذير الكاذبة كغيرهم ولكن اعترفوا على أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source reports that seven of ten tied themselves up; after returning and praying, the Prophet waited for God's command, released them after revelation, declined their offered wealth, and then 9:103 was revealed.
rows.anchor: وكانوا عشرة فسبعة منهم لما بلغهم ما نزل فى المتخلفين أوثقوا أنفسهم على سوارى المسجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good deed may mean going out for jihad, with the bad deed meaning staying behind; alternatively, they mixed repentance with sin.
rows.anchor: خروجا إلى الجهاد ﴿ وآخر سيئا ﴾ تخلفا عنه أو التوبة والاثم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conjunction wāw may carry the sense of bāʾ because conjunction and attachment are compatible.
rows.anchor: فالواو بمعنى الباء لأن الواو للجمع والباء للالصاق فيتناسبان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the wāw means each deed was mixed with the other, unlike saying water was mixed with milk, which makes only the water mixed into the milk.
rows.anchor: المعنى خلط كل واحد منهما بالآخر فكل واحد منهما مخلوط ومخلوط به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentary does not separately state that they repented because their confession of sins itself indicates repentance.
rows.anchor: ولم يذكر توبتهم لأنه ذكر اعترافهم بذنوبهم وهو دليل على التوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Makkī retains the yāʾ; Abū ʿAmr, Nāfiʿ, and ʿAlī agree in connected reading. Retention is original, while omission for the kasra is common in Hudhayl; the example is 18:64.
rows.anchor: والياء مكى وافقه أبو عمرو ونافع وعلى فى الوصل وإثبات الياء هو الأصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The subject of yaʾti refers to the day on which all people are gathered, not to the day grammatically annexed to yaʾti; yawm is governed by udhkur or lā takallamu.
rows.anchor: وفاعل يأت ضمير يرجع إلى قوله يوم مجموع له الناس لا اليوم المضاف إلى يأت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one intercedes except by God's permission, as in the verse asking who can intercede with Him except by His leave.
rows.anchor: أى لا يشفع أحد إلا بإذن الله من ذا الذى يشفع عنده إلا بإذنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to the people at the gathering, indicated by the preceding statement that no soul speaks and the earlier mention of all people; the wretched are punished and the happy blessed.
rows.anchor: الضمير لأهل الموقف لدلالة لا تكلم نفس عليه وقد مر ذكر الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zafīr is the donkey's first bray and shahīq its last; alternatively, they are the expelling and drawing back of breath.
rows.anchor: هو أول نهيق الحمار ﴿ وشهيق ﴾ هو آخره أو هما إخراج النفس ورده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is circumstantial, governed by the implicit existential in fī al-nār.
rows.anchor: والجملة فى موضع الحال والعامل فيها الاستقرار الذى فى النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥamza, ʿAlī, and Ḥafṣ read saʿidū with saʿida as an intransitive form; saʿadahu yasʿaduhu is transitive.
rows.anchor: سعدوا حمزة وعلى وحفص سعد لازم وسعده يسعده متعد

words: خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا مَا دَامَتِ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتُ وَٱلْأَرْضُ إِلَّا مَا شَآءَ رَبُّكَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation makes the exception refer to what is greater than Paradise's bliss: seeing God and His good pleasure.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن لهم سوى الجنة ما هو اكبر منها وهو رؤية الله تعالى ورضوانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God may punish a sinner for the measure of his sin before admitting him to Paradise.
rows.anchor: أو معناهاإلا من شاء أن يعذبه بقدر ذنبه قبل أن يدخله الجنة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra reports from the Prophet that the exception in both verses concerns Paradise's people: sinful Muslims do not remain eternally in Hell, and do not remain eternally in Paradise without having entered it.
rows.anchor: عن أبى هريرة رضى الله عنه عن النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال الاستثناء فى الآيتين لأهل الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Muʿtazila reject the transmitted reports because they deny that sinners leave Hell; the author calls this a manifest sin.
rows.anchor: والمعتزلة لما لم يروا خروج العصاة من النار ردوا الأحاديث المروية فى هذا الباب وكفى به اثما مبينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gift is not cut off but continues without end, as with the unending reward in 41:8.
rows.anchor: غير مقطوع ولكنه ممتد إلى غير نهاية كقوله لهم أجر غير ممنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾan is an accusative verbal noun, meaning that they were given a gift.
rows.anchor: وهو نصب فى المصدر أى اعطوا عطاء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A report says the Jahmiyya disbelieved four verses: the enduring fruit, God's enduring bounty, and provision that is neither cut off nor withheld, alongside this verse.
rows.anchor: قيل كفرت الجهمية بأربع آيات عطاء غير مجذوذ أكلها دائم وما عند الله باق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lawlā here is an exhortation or rebuke and is used specifically with a verb.
rows.anchor: فهلا كان هو موضوع للتحضيض ومخصوص بالفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ūlū baqiyya means people of virtue and goodness; the name comes from a person keeping the best of what he gives away, and the proverb calls the best remnants.
rows.anchor: أولو فضل وخير وسمى الفضل والجودة بقية لأن الرجل يستبقى مما يخرجه اجوده وأفضله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muḥammad and his community should wonder that among the nations destroyed in this sūra there were so few people of reason and religion who forbade disbelief and sins.
rows.anchor: عجب محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وأمته إن لم يكن فى الأمم التى ذكر الله اهلاكهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is disconnected: rather, a few of those saved forbade corruption, while the rest left the prohibition undone.
rows.anchor: استثناء منقطع أى ولكن قليلا ممن انجينا من القرون نهوا عن الفساد وسائرهم تاركون لللنهى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min is explanatory, not partitive, since only those who forbade evil were saved, as stated in 7:165.
rows.anchor: ومن فى ممن انجينا للبيان لا للتبعيض لأن النجاة للناهين وحدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who wronged are the people who abandoned forbidding evil; the clause coordinates with the implied account that a few forbade it, and they followed their desires.
rows.anchor: أى التاركون للنهى عن المنكر وهو عطف على ممضمر أى إلا قليلا ممن انجينا منهم نهوا عن الفساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They pursued luxury: love of leadership and wealth and the means to an easy life, abandoning the command to enjoin good and forbid evil.
rows.anchor: من حب الرياسة والثروة وطلب أسباب العيش الهنيء ورفضوا الأمر بالمعروف والنهى عن المنكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final phrase is parenthetical and judges them to be criminals.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وكانوا مجرمين ﴾ اعتراض وحكم عليهم بأنهم قوم مجرمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unseen is what is hidden from creation, and the visible is what they witness.
rows.anchor: ﴿ عالم الغيب ﴾ ما غاب عن الخلق ﴿ والشهادة ﴾ ما شاهدوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Kabīr means immense in rank, with everything beneath Him.
rows.anchor: العظيم الشأن الذي كل شيء دونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Mutaʿāl means either above everything by His power or exalted beyond the attributes of creatures.
rows.anchor: المستعلى على كل شيء بقدرته أو الذي كبر عن صفات المخلوقين وتعالى عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Makkī reads with yāʾ in both forms of the final pair of divine names.
rows.anchor: وبالياء فى الحالين مكى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who speak secretly or aloud, hide at night, or go openly by day are equal in God's knowledge.
rows.anchor: ﴿ سواء منكم من أسر القول ومن جهر به ﴾ أي في علمه ﴿ ومن هو مستخف بالليل ﴾ متوار ﴿ وسارب بالنهار ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mustakhfin is one who conceals himself; sā rib is one who goes along his way, from saraba in the land, meaning to travel.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ومن هو مستخف بالليل ﴾ متوار ﴿ وسارب بالنهار ﴾ ذاهب في سربه أي في طريقه ووجهه يقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sārib may coordinate with the full relative clause man huwa mustakhfin, not with mustakhfin alone; alternatively, it coordinates with mustakhfin, with man carrying a dual sense.
rows.anchor: سارب عطف على من هو مستخف لا على مستخف أو على مستخف غير أن من في معنى الاثنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kitāb is the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning this Book, namely the sūra; the clause anzalnāhu ilayka is an adjectival clause in the nominative.
rows.anchor: ﴿ الر كتاب ﴾ هو خبر مبتدأ محذوف أي هذا كتاب يعنى السورة والجملة التي هي ﴿ أنزلناه إليك ﴾

words: لِتُخْرِجَ ٱلنَّاسَ مِنَ ٱلظُّلُمَٰتِ إِلَى ٱلنُّورِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet brings people from error to guidance by calling them.
rows.anchor: ﴿ لتخرج الناس ﴾ بدعائك اياهم ﴿ من الظلمات إلى النور ﴾ من الضلالة إلى الهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By their Lord's permission means by His enabling and easing their way, metaphorically likened to permission that opens a curtain.
rows.anchor: ﴿ بإذن ربهم ﴾ بتيسيره وتسهيله مستعار من الاذن الذي هو تسهيل الحجاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase to the path substitutes for the light, with the governing preposition repeated.
rows.anchor: بدل من النور بتكرير العامل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿAzīz is the one who prevails in retribution; al-Ḥamīd is praised for beneficence.
rows.anchor: ﴿ العزيز ﴾ الغالب بالانتقام ﴿ الحميد ﴾ المحمود على الانعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening means: remember when Abraham said this prayer.
rows.anchor: واذكر إذ قال إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the sacred city. Unlike 2:126, Abraham now asks that a city already characterized by fear be turned into a safe one, rather than merely included among safe cities.
rows.anchor: الفرق بين هذه وبين ما في البقرة أنه قد سأل فيها أن يجعل من جملة البلدان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ajunibnī means distance me from idol worship and keep me continually avoiding it, as in the prayer to make us Muslims to You.
rows.anchor: وبعدنى أي ثبتنى وأدمنى على اجتناب عبادتها كما قال واجعلنا مسلمين لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By his sons Abraham meant his biological sons.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وبني ﴾ أراد بنيه من صلبه

words: رَبِّ إِنَّهُنَّ أَضْلَلْنَ كَثِيرًۭا مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols caused people to go astray: people strayed because of them, so the idols are spoken of as if they themselves led people astray.
rows.anchor: جعلن مضلات على طريق التسبيب لأن الناس ضلوا بسببهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever follows Abraham's religion as a sincere monotheist is of him, meaning like a part of him through their close bond.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فمن تبعني ﴾ على ملتى وكان حنيفا مسلما مثلى ﴿ فإنه مني ﴾ أي هو بعضى لفرط اختصاصه بي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If disobedience means anything short of associating partners with God, Abraham asks God to forgive that disobedient person.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ومن عصانى ﴾ فيما دون الشرك ﴿ فإنك غفور رحيم ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, whoever disobeys by committing shirk is forgiven if he repents and believes.
rows.anchor: أو ومن عصانى عصيان شرك فإنك غفور رحيم ان تاب وآمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The descendants Abraham settled were some of his children: Ishmael and his descendants.
rows.anchor: بعض أولادى وهم إسماعيل ومن ولد منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The valley is Mecca, where nothing grows at all.
rows.anchor: ﴿ بواد ﴾ هو وادى مكة ﴿ غير ذي زرع ﴾ لا يكون فيه شيء من زرع قط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Sacred House is named so because God forbade treating it carelessly and made its surroundings sacred for its sake.
rows.anchor: لأن الله تعالى حرم التعرض له والتهاون به وجعل ما حوله حرما لمكانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it is named because it has always been protected from every tyrant.
rows.anchor: أو لأنه لم يزل ممنعا يها به كل جبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it is revered and possesses a great sanctity that may not be violated.
rows.anchor: أو لأنه محترم عظيم الحرمة لا يحل انتهاكها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it is protected from the flood, just as it is called ʿAtīq because it was freed from it.
rows.anchor: أو لأنه حرم على الطوفان أي منع منه كما سمى عتيقا لأنه أعتق منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose phrase li-yuqīmū is attached to askantu: Abraham settled them in the barren valley solely to establish prayer at the Sacred House and maintain it through worship and remembrance.
rows.anchor: اللام متعلقة باسكنت أي ما اسكنتهم بهذا الوادى البلقع إلا ليقيموا الصلاة عند بيتك المحرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min is partitive: Abraham asks for some human hearts, since asking for all hearts would have brought Persians, Romans, Turks, and Indians to crowd the place.
rows.anchor: ومن للتبعيض لما روى عن مجاهد لو قال أفئدة الناس لزاحمتكم عليه فارس والروم والترك والهند

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says that had Abraham asked for all people's hearts, Persians, Romans, Turks, and Indians would have crowded there.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد لو قال أفئدة الناس لزاحمتكم عليه فارس والروم والترك والهند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min may instead mark origin, as in saying my heart is sick; the phrase then means people's hearts, with the possessor indefinite to match the indefinite afʾida.
rows.anchor: أو للابتداء كقولك القلب منى سقيم تريد قلبى فكانه قيل أفئدة ناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hearts rush to Abraham's descendants from distant lands, flying toward them with longing.
rows.anchor: تسرع اليهم من البلاد الشاسعة وتطير نحوهم شوقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although they live in a valley with no fruit, God supplies them by bringing fruit from faraway lands.
rows.anchor: مع سكناهم واديا ما فيه شيء منها بأن تجلب إليهم من البلاد الشاسعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They may give thanks for the provision of many kinds of fruit in a valley without trees or water.
rows.anchor: النعمة في أن يرزقوا أنواع الثمرات في واد ليس فيه شجر ولا ماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the address Rabbana signals supplication and appeal to God.
rows.anchor: النداء المكرر دليل التضرع واللجأ إلى الله

words: إِنَّكَ تَعْلَمُ مَا نُخْفِى وَمَا نُعْلِنُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows what is secret just as He knows what is public.
rows.anchor: تعلم السر كما تعلم العلن

words: وَمَا يَخْفَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ مِن شَىْءٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that nothing on earth or in heaven is hidden may be God's speech, confirming Abraham's words.
rows.anchor: من كلام الله عز وجل تصديقا لإبراهيم عليه السلام

words: وَمَا يَخْفَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ مِن شَىْءٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the statement may continue as Abraham's speech.
rows.anchor: أو من كلام إبراهيم

words: مِن شَىْءٍۢ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَلَا فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min is comprehensive: nothing whatsoever is hidden from God.
rows.anchor: ومن للاستغراق كأنه قيل وما يخفى على الله شيء ما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham asks for some of his descendants to establish prayer, since God had informed him that unbelievers would occur among them.
rows.anchor: وبعض ذريتى عطفا على المنصوب في اجعلنى وإنما بعض لانه علم باعلام الله أنه يكون في ذريته كفار

rows.speaker: ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says that people of Abraham's descendants will remain upon the natural faith until the Hour.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما لا يزال من ولد إبراهيم ناس على الفطرة إلى ان تقوم الساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Makkī retains yāʾ in duʿāʾ at pause and connection; Abū ʿAmr and Ḥamza retain it in connection, while the others omit it.
rows.anchor: بالياء في الوصل والوقف مكى وافقه أبو عمرو وحمزة في الوصل الباقون بلاياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The request means either answer my prayer or accept my worship.
rows.anchor: أي استجب دعائى أو عبادتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threatened day is the Resurrection; alternatively, it is their immediate destruction by torment, or their death amid agony and meeting angels without good news.
rows.anchor: أي يوم القيامة ويوم مفعول ثان لأنذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawm is the second object of warn, not a time adverb, since the warning does not occur on that day.
rows.anchor: ويوم مفعول ثان لأنذر لا ظرف إذ الانذار لا يكون في ذلك اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who did wrong are the unbelievers.
rows.anchor: أي الكفار

words: رَبَّنَآ أَخِّرْنَآ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍۢ قَرِيبٍۢ نُّجِبْ دَعْوَتَكَ وَنَتَّبِعِ ٱلرُّسُلَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They beg to return to worldly life and receive a short reprieve so they can make up for failing to answer God's call and follow the messengers.
rows.anchor: أي ردنا إلى الدنيا وامهلنا إلى أمد وحد من الزمان قريب نتدارك ما فرطنا فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reply recalls their worldly oath that they would not be moved from their state: they denied resurrection, as in 16:38.
rows.anchor: حلفتم في الدنيا انكم إذا متم لا تزالون عن تلك الحالة ولا تنتقلون إلى دار أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the answer to their oath; the direct second-person wording replaces their original first-person words, as with the quoted form aqsa mtum.
rows.anchor: وما لكم جواب القسم وإنما جاء بلفظ الخطاب كقوله اقسمتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speakers are the unbelievers; al-dhikr means the Qurʾān, and they address Muḥammad as one to whom it was sent down.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وقالوا ﴾ أي الكفار ﴿ يا أيها الذي نزل عليه الذكر ﴾ أي القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The taunt is mockery: they acknowledge the Qurʾān's descent while calling Muḥammad mad, deliberately reversing their words to ridicule him and saying he speaks like a madman when he claims revelation.
rows.anchor: وكيف يقرون بنزول الذكر عليه وينسبونه إلى الجنون والتعكيس في كلامهم للاستهزاء والتهكم سائغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentary compares this taunt with Pharaoh's charge of madness and with other sarcastic Qurʾānic expressions.
rows.anchor: كما قال فرعون ان رسولكم الذي ارسل اليكم لمجنون وكيف يقرون بنزول الذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-dhikr is the Qurʾān; the preservation promise answers the unbelievers' denial and mockery in 15:6.
rows.anchor: وهو رد لانكارهم واستهزائهم في قولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God preserves the Qurʾān from satans and at all times from addition, subtraction, distortion, and alteration.
rows.anchor: محفوظا من الشياطين وهو حافظه في كل وقت من الزيادة والنقصان والتحريف والتبديل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier scriptures were entrusted to rabbis and scholars rather than divinely preserved; their envy-driven disputes led to distortion, whereas the Qurʾān was not left in others' care.
rows.anchor: فإنه لم يتول حفظها وإنما استحفظها الربانيين والاحبار فاختلفوا فيما بينهم بغيا فوقع التحريف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's preservation is evidence that the Qurʾān was revealed by Him: human speech would be vulnerable to additions and omissions.
rows.anchor: دليلا على أنه منزل من عنده آية اذ لو كان من قول البشر أو غير آية لتطرق عليه الزيادة والنقصان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the pronoun refers to the Messenger, as in God's promise to protect him.
rows.anchor: أو الضمير في له لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كقوله والله يعصمك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When God completed and formed Adam, He prepared him to receive the spirit.
rows.anchor: خلقته وهيأتها لنفخ الروح فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spirit means that God gave Adam life; there was no literal blowing, which is figurative, and the possessive phrase marks special attribution.
rows.anchor: وجعلت فيه الروح وأحييته وليس ثمت نفخ وإنما هو تمثيل والاضافة للتخصيص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waqaʿa means fall, here to prostrate; the fāʾ makes the command the answer to idhā, showing a command may precede its time of action.
rows.anchor: هو أمر من وقع يقع أي اسقطوا على الأرض يعنى اسجدوا له ودخل الفاء لأنه جواب إذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The creator is God and the one who does not create is the idols.
rows.anchor: ﴿ أفمن يخلق ﴾ أي الله تعالى ﴿ كمن لا يخلق ﴾ أي الأصنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Man, normally for rational beings, is used because the idolaters named and worshipped idols as gods; alternatively, the comparison first means one rational creator is unlike a rational noncreator, much less an unintelligent object.
rows.anchor: وجىء بمن الذي هو لأولى العلم لزعمهم حيث سموها آلهة وعبدوها فاجروها مجرى أولى العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording reverses the surface expectation to refute idolaters who equate idols with God: by making idols God's equals, they make God like created things, so the verse denies that a creator resembles a noncreator.
rows.anchor: وانما لم يقل أفمن لا يخلق كمن يخلق مع اقتضاء المقام بظاهره إياه لكونه الزاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is an argument against the Muʿtazila concerning the creation of acts.
rows.anchor: وهو حجة على المعتزلة في خلق الأفعال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing question urges them to recognize the error of their position.
rows.anchor: فتعرفون فساد ما أنتم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those the unbelievers call upon apart from God are the idols.
rows.anchor: يدعوهم الكفار ﴿ من دون الله ﴾ وبالتاء غير عاصم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All readers other than ʿĀṣim read the verb with tāʾ.
rows.anchor: وبالتاء غير عاصم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols create nothing and are themselves created.
rows.anchor: لا يخلقون شيئا وهم يخلقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What you have is the world's transient goods; what is with God is His everlasting store of mercy.
rows.anchor: اعراض الدنيا ﴿ ينفد وما عند الله ﴾ من خزائن رحمته ﴿ باق ﴾ لا ينفد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Makkī and ʿĀṣim read the verb with nūn; the other readers use yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وبالنون مكى وعاصم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who endured the unbelievers' persecution and Islam's hardships receive their reward according to the best of their deeds.
rows.anchor: ﴿ الذين صبروا ﴾ على أذى المشركين ومشاق الاسلام ﴿ أجرهم بأحسن ما كانوا يعملون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Ṭā Hā enumerates disconnected letter names, this begins a new statement.
rows.anchor: ان جعلت طه تعديدا لاسماء الحروف فهو ابتداء كلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Ṭā Hā names the sūra, the clause may predicate of it with the sūra as subject; al-Qurʾān appears overtly instead of a pronoun because the sūra is Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: احتملت أن تكون خبرا عنها وهي في موضع المبتدأ والقرآن ظاهرا وقع موقع المضمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the statement is the response to an oath treating Ṭā Hā as its subject.
rows.anchor: وأن يكون جوابا لها وهي قسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is not to exhaust himself in grief over the unbelievers and their refusal to believe, or through night worship.
rows.anchor: لتتعب لفرط تأسفك عليهم وعلى كفرهم وتحسرك على ان يؤمنوا أو بقيام الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet prayed at night until his feet swelled, and Gabriel told him to spare himself because his soul had rights; revelation did not come to exhaust him, and his mission is the easy, upright religion.
rows.anchor: وأنه روى أنه عليه السلام صلى بالليل حت تورمت قدماه فقال له جبريل ابق على نفسك فان لها عليك حقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is disconnected, meaning rather it was sent as a reminder; alternatively, the phrase is circumstantial.
rows.anchor: استثناء منقطع أي لكن انزلناه تذكرة أو حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder is for one who fears God, or whose eventual outcome is fear.
rows.anchor: لمن يخاف الله أو لمن يؤل أمره إلى الخشية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tajhar means to raise your voice.
rows.anchor: ترفع صوتك ﴿ فإنه يعلم السر ﴾ ما أسررته إلى غيرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sirr is what you disclose privately to another; akhfā is either a thought occurring in your mind or something you will later conceal within yourself.
rows.anchor: ما أسررته في نفسك وما ستسره فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship God by affirming His oneness and obeying Him.
rows.anchor: وحدني واطعني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means to remember God in prayer because prayer contains invocations.
rows.anchor: لتذكرني فيها لاشتمال الصلاة على الأدكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the prayer is for God's remembrance because He mentioned and commanded it in the scriptures.
rows.anchor: أو لأني ذكرتها في الكتب وأمرت بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, prayer is so that God may remember the worshipper with praise.
rows.anchor: أو لأن أذكرك بالمدح والثناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it is for God's remembrance alone, without mixing in remembrance of anyone else.
rows.anchor: أو لذكري خاصة لا تشوبه بذكر غيري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it means that the worshipper should remember God without forgetting Him.
rows.anchor: أو لتكون لي ذاكرا غير ناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it means at the times of God's remembrance, namely the prayer times, as in 4:103.
rows.anchor: أو لأوقات ذكري وهي مواقيت الصلاة لقوله إن الصلاة كانت على المؤمنين كتابا موقوتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It has also been interpreted as praying after forgetting; this requires ellipsis of the annexed noun, meaning remembrance of my prayer.
rows.anchor: وقد حمل على ذكر الصلاة بعد نسيانها وذا يصح بتقدير حذف المضاف أي لذكر صلاتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shows that no obligatory act after monotheism is greater than prayer.
rows.anchor: وهذا دليل على أنه لا فريضة بعد التوحيد أعظم منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā is the subject and tilka its predicate, meaning hādhihi; bi-yamīnika is circumstantial and can mean resting in or held by the right hand, or tilka may be a relative pronoun with bi-yamīnika as its clause.
rows.anchor: ما مبتدأ وتلك خبره هي بمعنى هذه وبيمينك حال عمل فيها معنى الإشارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's question draws Moses' attention before the miracle, acclimates him to the staff becoming a snake, or comforts him and removes fear before the conversation.
rows.anchor: والسؤال للتنبيه لتقع المعجزة بها بعد التثبت أو للتوطين لئلا يهول انقلابها حية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses leaned on the staff when tired, when standing at the head of the flock, and when leaping.
rows.anchor: اعتمد عليها إذا أعييت أو وقفت على رأس القطيع وعند الطفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He shook tree branches with it so their leaves would fall for his sheep to eat.
rows.anchor: أخبط ورق الشجر على غنمي لتأكل

rows.speaker: حفص
rows.claim: The text identifies Ḥafṣ's reading at wa-lī fīhā.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ولي فيها ﴾ حفص ﴿ مآرب ﴾ جمع مأربة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maʾārib is the plural of maʾriba, which has three possible vowelings and means needs.
rows.anchor: جمع مأربة بالحركات الثلاثة وهي بالحاجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine ukhrā differs from the expected masculine ukhar because it refers to a plural collective or matches the verse endings, as with al-kubrā.
rows.anchor: والقياس اخر وإنما قال أخرى ردا إلى الجماعة أو لنسق الآي وكذا الكبرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The staff also walked and spoke with him, fought enemies and beasts, became a well rope and bucket, gave light, carried provisions, grew fruit, brought water, and warded off vermin.
rows.anchor: والمآرب الآخر أنها كانت تماشيه وتحدثه وتحارب العدو والسباع وتصير رشاء فتطول بطول البئر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His added details either express gratitude while he mentions some benefits and modestly leaves the rest, or answer an implied second question about what he does with the staff.
rows.anchor: والزيادة على الجواب لتعداد النعم شكرا أو لأنها جواب سؤال آخر لأنه لما قال هي عصاي قيل له ما تصنع بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' fear had so subsided that he put his hand into the snake's mouth and took it by its jaws.
rows.anchor: بلغ من ذهاب خوفه أن أدخل يده في فمها وأخذ بلحييها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sīra is the state a person is in, natural or acquired; it originally derives from a word for walking and came to mean condition or way. Here God returns the snake to its first state as a staff.
rows.anchor: والسيرة الحالة التي يكون عليها الانسان غريزية كانت أو مكتسبة وهي في الأصل فعلة من السير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sīratahā is adverbial, meaning He will restore it to its first manner or condition, as it was when a staff.
rows.anchor: وانتصبت على الظرف أي سنعيدها في طريقتها الأولى أي في حال ما كانت عصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God showed this to Moses during the conversation so he would not be frightened when the staff became a snake before Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: وأرى ذلك موسى عند المخاطبة لئلا يفزع منها إذا انقلبت حية عند فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Make easy the task commanded of me: delivering the message to Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: وسهل ما أمرتني به من تبليغ الرسالة إلى فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Make my affair easy reinforces expand my chest by repeating its meaning first generally and then specifically; naming chest and affair clarifies what is to be expanded and eased.
rows.anchor: أكد من اشرح صدري لانه تكرير للمعنى الواحد من طريقي الاجمالي والتفصيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's signs are His miracles.
rows.anchor: ﴿ اذهب أنت وأخوك بآياتي ﴾ بمعجزاتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not grow slack: wanā means weakness and falling short.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ولا تنيا ﴾ تفترا من الوني وهو الفتور والتقصير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's remembrance may be the wing on which they fly, or may mean conveying the message, the greatest of the acts of worship.
rows.anchor: أي اتخذا ذكري جناحا تطيران به أو أريد بالذكر تبليغ الرسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity was created from earth through its father Adam.
rows.anchor: من الأرض خلقناكم أي أباكم آدم عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, each drop of semen is mixed with earth from its burial place, so human beings are formed from both soil and semen.
rows.anchor: يعجن كل نطفة بشيء من تراب مدفنه فيخلق من التراب والنطفة معا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, semen comes from foods, and foods come from the earth.
rows.anchor: أو لأن النطفة من الاغذية وهي من الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God returns people to the earth when they die and are buried.
rows.anchor: إذا متم فدفنتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At resurrection, God reassembles scattered parts mixed into earth, restores them alive, and brings them to the assembly.
rows.anchor: أنه يؤلف اجزاءهم المتفرقة المختلطة بالتراب ويردهم كما كانوا أحياء ويخرجهم إلى المحشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth serves as a bed and cradle, offers paths and plants for human food and animal fodder, is humanity's origin and mother, and receives the dead.
rows.anchor: جعلها لهم فراشا ومهادا يتقلبون عليها وسوى لهم فيها مسالك يترددون فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses addresses the sorcerers.
rows.anchor: أي للسحرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He tells them not to falsely call God's signs and miracles sorcery.
rows.anchor: لا تدعوا آياته ومعجزاته سحرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kufis other than Abū Bakr use the form yushitukum; the others have fatḥa on yāʾ and ḥāʾ. Both forms mean destroy or annihilate.
rows.anchor: كوفي غير أبي بكر يهلككم وبفتح الياء والحاء غيرهم والسحت والاسحاق بمعنى الإعدام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is in the subjunctive as the result of the prohibition.
rows.anchor: وبفتح الياء والحاء غيرهم والسحت والاسحاق بمعنى الإعدام وانتصب على جواب النهى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever lies about God has failed.
rows.anchor: من كذب على الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means decide upon your scheme and make it unanimous so you will not disagree.
rows.anchor: فاحكموا أي جعلوه مجمعا عليه حتى لا تختلفوا

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads fa-ijmaʿū, supported by the wording fa-jamaʿa kaydahu in 54:44.
rows.anchor: فاجمعوا أبو عمرو ويعضده فجمع كيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kayd means the means used to scheme.
rows.anchor: هو ما يكاد به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are to come arranged in a row; ṣaffan is a circumstantial accusative.
rows.anchor: مصطفين حال أمر وابان يأتوا صفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arriving in ranks is more fearsome to those watching.
rows.anchor: لانه أهيب في صدور الرائين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing clause means whoever prevails today has succeeded and is parenthetical.
rows.anchor: وقد فاز من غلب وهو اعتراض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-aʿlā means the victor and dominant one.
rows.anchor: الغالب القاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle inna, the pronoun anta, the definite article, and the word al-ʿulūw intensify the assertion of manifest superiority.
rows.anchor: وفي ذكر أن وأنت وحرف التعريف ولفظ العلو وهو الغلبة الظاهرة مبالغة بينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lan nuʾthiraka means we will not choose or prefer you.
rows.anchor: لن نختارك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clear proofs are decisive signs that show Moses is truthful.
rows.anchor: القاطعة الدالة على صدق موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may coordinate with what came to them, so they will not prefer Pharaoh over revelation or their Creator; alternatively, it is an oath with the response lan nuʾthiraka placed before it.
rows.anchor: عطف على ما جاءنا أي لن نختارك على الذي جاءنا ولا على الذي خلقنا أو قسم وجوابه لن يؤثر مقدم على القسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They tell Pharaoh to do whatever he will, including killing or persecuting them; alternatively, qāḍin means decide or judge. The cited line قضاهما is glossed as making or completing.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فاقض ما أنت قاض ﴾ فاصنع ما أنت صانع من القتل والطلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The quoted poetic word قضاهما can mean he made or completed them, supporting the sense of doing what one intends.
rows.anchor: وعليهما مسرودتان قضاهما أي صنعهما أو أحكم ما أنت حاكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means in this worldly life; the words are an adverb of time, limiting Pharaoh's power over them to their lifetime.
rows.anchor: أي في هذه الحياة الدنيا فانتصب على الظروف أي إنما تحكم فينا مدة حياتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā is a relative pronoun, the object coordinated with our sins; min al-siḥr is a circumstantial phrase modifying it.
rows.anchor: ﴿ إنا آمنا بربنا ليغفر لنا خطايانا وما أكرهتنا عليه ﴾ ما موصولة منصوبة بالعطف على خطايانا ﴿ من السحر ﴾ حال من ما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the sorcerers saw Moses guarded by his staff while asleep, recognized that this was no ordinary magic, and feared exposure; Pharaoh compelled them to perform magic, harming himself through ignorance while their knowledge benefited them.
rows.anchor: روى أنهم قالوا لفرعون أرنا موسى نائما ففعل فوجدوه وتحرسه عصاه فقالوا ما هذا بسحر الساحر إذا نام بطل سحره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives the better reward to the obedient and the more lasting punishment to the disobedient, rebutting Pharaoh's threat in 20:71.
rows.anchor: ﴿ والله خير ﴾ ثوابا لمن أطاعه ﴿ وأبقى ﴾ عقاب المن عصاه وهو رد لقول فرعون ولتعلمن أينا أشد عذابا وأبقى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Innahu contains the pronoun of the matter.
rows.anchor: هو ضمير الشأن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here a criminal means an unbeliever; lahu refers to that criminal.
rows.anchor: ﴿ من يأت ربه مجرما ﴾ كافرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He does not die and gain relief through death, nor live a life from which he can benefit.
rows.anchor: فيستربح بالموت ﴿ ولا يحيى ﴾ حياة ينتفع بها
